description: Hand-labelled census of every compatible stored NVDA analysis, used as an in-sample regression pin for the deterministic materiality gate, its grouping arms, and its ranking. Titles, publishers, URLs, timestamps, Stage A fields, Stage B claim verdicts, and evidence references are verbatim projections of the stored analyses; fields no materiality rule reads (Stage A summary text, Stage B reasoning, evidence strength) are not carried, and are filled with named placeholders on reconstruction. This is a materiality judgement and is not the selector gold set.
labelling_rules: Material: the development changes an identifiable driver of the company's future cash flows or risk profile, persists beyond the news cycle, and is evidenced by a source with direct knowledge or independent corroboration. All three must hold.

Evidence is part of the definition, not only of the gate: an issuer's own announcement of a product launch or a partnership is a statement of intent, so it is labelled immaterial unless something outside the company's channels reports it. An issuer is first-hand on its own money and its own obligations, so its investments, acquisitions, financings, and results stand alone.

A headline that leads with a share-price or market-value move is a price reaction and never material, even when a real event appears in its cause clause. This follows the convention already pinned in nvda_selector_gold.json.

Third-party subjects are immaterial: another company's financing, project, or product, with this company named only as the technology involved. An industry-level shift in how demand for this company's products is served is material.
Talks are material when the reported transaction is concrete -- a named counterparty and a named action or size -- and immaterial when only an unspecified deal is reported.

group_id names the announcement or action a row reports, so two outlets covering one announcement share it. A follow-up that discloses new terms a day later is a different development and gets its own id. Immaterial rows carry null.

corpus.note: The census is ordered as the product loads it: published_at descending, then stored analysis recency. Grouping and ranking are deterministic for this order. 119 rows were labelled on 2026-08-25; the six rows a later collection run added were labelled on 2026-08-26 under the same rules, and none of the original labels was revisited.
